youtube.title: Radar Saw the Pearl Harbor Attack Coming 53 Minutes Early. Here's What Happened
youtube.description:
At 7:02 a.m. on 7 December 1941, Army privates Joseph Lockard and George Elliott spotted the biggest radar contact they had ever seen, about 130 miles north of Oahu. The duty officer, expecting American B-17s from California, told them not to worry. An hour earlier, USS Ward had fired on a Japanese submarine. At 7:55, the attack began. Investigators later cleared the officer: the radar could not tell friend from foe, and he had not been told of the war warning.

📂 Case File #044: The Pearl Harbor Radar
